title: Overnight pulse oximetry
what: At home, you sleep with a small sensor on your finger. It records your blood oxygen and pulse all night.
why: For snoring, pauses in breathing during sleep, daytime sleepiness, lung or heart disease, or to set up oxygen therapy.
duration: one night at home; the report is usually ready in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you snore or stop breathing during sleep
If you take sleeping pills or sedatives
If you need oxygen at night
If you have lung or heart disease

prepare.title: Nails
prepare.text: Remove nail polish and fake nails from the finger the sensor will go on.

prepare.title: Evening
prepare.text: No alcohol and no extra coffee in the evening.

prepare.title: Sleep
prepare.text: Sleep as usual, in your own bed.

bring: The device and instructions the clinic gives you
steps: At the clinic, you get the device and are shown how to put it on
Before bed, you put the sensor on your finger
You turn on the device and go to sleep as usual
If the sensor falls off at night, put it back on
In the morning, you take it off and turn it off
You return the device to the clinic
feel: It does not hurt. The sensor is just a clip
Sleeping with it feels odd at first
after: Return the device by the time the clinic tells you
The report is usually ready in 1 to 3 days
If needed, your doctor will suggest a full sleep study
red_flags: Severe shortness of breath, blue lips, or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.q: What if the sensor falls off at night?
faq.a: Put it back on. Short gaps usually do not matter, but tell the clinic about them.

faq.q: Does this replace a sleep study?
faq.a: Not fully. It is a simple first step. Sometimes a full sleep study is needed after it.

reminders.text: Overnight pulse oximetry tonight. Remove polish from your finger, put the sensor on before bed, and turn on the device.
